result.architecture_summary: A layered pipeline: immutable point-in-time Reconciliation (GDD vs repo) feeds a persisted, schema-2.0 task-contract graph (`Tasks/*.yaml`) that defines work but no longer carries mutable completion status. Evidence-derived conformance (`Pipeline/TaskGraph/current_conformance.py`) reads committed Git history plus immutable delivery/revalidation records to answer "is this task currently conformant," deliberately separated from an `execution_authority` gate that currently denies all dispatch. A new provider-neutral `AgentRuntime` (Stage 3-4D) wraps Claude Code and OpenAI/Codex behind a generic `AgentInvocationRequest`, with a planned separate `TaskExecution` layer for NSC-specific identity (not yet implemented/consumed). The only production consumer of AgentRuntime so far is a self-review tool (`ArchitectureReview`) that runs 8 reviewer roles + synthesis + adversarial critique against each provider, read-only. GER (Generate→Evaluate→Refine→Circuit-Breaker) with runtime-evidence feedback is the intended execution-validation loop, proven only in prior coursework (Assignment 6), not yet under the new contract/evidence model.
result.verdict_reason: Individually, most mechanisms are reasonable responses to real, previously-observed failures (fake completion via YAML edit, static-pass/runtime-fail camera bug, unbounded LLM planning drift). But the system as it stands today has zero write capability for any provider (`repository_write` and `approved_command_execution` are hard-forbidden in the live Claude adapter; Codex is empty-capability only), has never executed a single ticket end-to-end under its own new contract/evidence/AgentRuntime model, and has spent its entire recent working window (2026-08-21 to 2026-08-23) building and then re-reviewing infrastructure that reviews itself (ArchitectureReview migrated to Claude, then to Codex, then to Claude again through AgentRuntime) rather than advancing NSC-003 or any gameplay ticket — directly contradicting the project's own stated rule (ADR-019 / "Current Development Rule") that infrastructure should be proven by advancing the actual game. The one delivered gameplay proof point, NSC-023, predates this entire apparatus and was validated retroactively by hand-authoring its evidence record, not produced by the pipeline. This is not simply "correct but oversized" — the critical-path capability (an agent that can write code and have that work objectively evidenced) does not exist, so the architecture cannot yet be judged as creating leverage; it has produced governance/audit machinery around a production loop that has never run once.
strong_decisions: Separating mutable task-contract definitions from immutable delivery/revalidation evidence (Phase 1-3, ADR-031/033) directly fixes a demonstrated exploit: a one-line YAML edit could previously fake completion and unlock downstream work.

Treating runtime Unity evidence as first-class validation input rather than trusting static/source-level evaluator success (ADR-015), based on the real Assignment 6 camera failure where static evaluation passed but the feature did not work.

Fail-closed provider capability enforcement (Claude/Codex adapters reject repository_write, approved_command_execution, non-null token_limit) prevents an unproven provider path from silently gaining destructive capability.
Branch/worktree isolation and 'done means merged' (ADR-006/007) are standard, appropriate safeguards against Unity scene/prefab merge hazards.
Deterministic-vs-LLM division of labor (graph computation, hashing, readiness are code; semantic judgment is the model) is the correct general principle for this kind of system.

Reading authority from committed Git HEAD rather than the working tree (Phase 3A) is a clean, testable trust boundary that was verified to behave correctly (uncommitted evidence ignored, then correctly flips state once committed).
structural_flaws: No provider can currently write to the repository or execute commands (repository_write and approved_command_execution are explicitly forbidden in the live Claude adapter; Codex supports only empty-capability or read/search). The elaborate AgentRuntime/provider-adapter investment therefore cannot yet be used to implement a single gameplay feature — only to read and critique.

The only real production consumer of AgentRuntime built so far is ArchitectureReview reviewing this same architecture, migrated twice (Codex, then Claude) in the last observed window. Infrastructure effort has been spent making the self-review loop more elaborate (provider-scoped outputs, resumability, adversarial critique of synthesis) rather than closing the execution loop.

taskcontrol ready and taskcontrol authorize are hard-denied for every task with no implemented dispatch policy, so the persistent graph, evidence model, and provider adapters currently cannot be chained into any actual autonomous or semi-autonomous execution, even for the task explicitly flagged as the anchor (NSC-003) three days ago.

NSC-003's task contract still declares decomposition_state: concrete and execution_scope: single_agent, while CURRENT_STATE.md separately says a human must first resolve six open design/arbitration questions before it can be handed to a worker — the persisted graph and the current human-facing narrative disagree about whether the task is actually ready, which is exactly the kind of graph-truth mismatch the mission brief warns against trusting.

No evidence-record generator exists; the one real conformance proof (NSC-023) required a human/manual process to hand-author the JSON binding commit, tree, gates, and artifacts. This is audit paperwork layered on manual work, not automation leverage, and does not obviously scale past one hand-built example.

Reconciliation/verification is built as a heavyweight, multi-model, independently-verified, immutable-snapshot process appropriate for a one-time bootstrap, but there is no implemented lightweight mechanism for the routine, scoped GDD-impact analysis the docs themselves say will eventually be needed as the GDD keeps changing during production.
observed_failure_solutions: Mutable YAML status could fake completion and unlock downstream dependencies without proof -> evidence-derived conformance records bound to Git commit/tree/blob hashes (Phase 1-3).
Assignment 6's camera passed static evaluation while being unusable in Play Mode -> runtime evidence is required as first-class validation input re-entering the Refiner loop (ADR-015).
Assignment 6 observed a Refiner claim 'implemented' while making no changes under Assets/ -> no-op refinements now explicitly count as failed progress against repair budget (ADR-016).
Reconciliation/Work Graph Seeder output could be stale relative to main -> old planning artifacts must be reconciled against current repository state before seeding (ADR-018).
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Full multi-provider AgentRuntime abstraction (Claude + Codex, capability mapping, turn-budget translation) exists before a single provider has ever completed one real write-capable implementation ticket; the cross-provider comparison this enables has no consumer yet.

TaskExecution as a layer separate from generic AgentRuntime (ADR-039) is designed and documented but has zero implemented consumers — it protects against a contamination problem (task semantics leaking into the generic runtime) that has not yet occurred because no task-bound execution exists.

Artifact Authority Gate, Progressive Decomposer, and the full Milestone-2 bundle (RAG + scanner + compact context + artifact authority) are specified in detail for a scenario (an autonomous agent inventing missing design) that has not yet been observed, while the simpler, already-observed problem (no write capability, no end-to-end ticket) remains unaddressed.

The immutable, multi-model-verified Reconciliation Verification Crew (coverage/structure/execution-scope auditors, streaming refinement, conflict arbitration) is built to guard against bad initial bootstrap seeding, a one-time event, at a level of rigor that would be prohibitively expensive to re-run for routine GDD iteration going forward.

Resumable, provider-scoped ArchitectureReview output layout (outputs/claude/, outputs/codex/, atomic LATEST.json pointer) anticipates a future Claude-vs-Codex comparison pipeline that does not exist and is not scheduled.
overengineering: Two full architecture-review provider migrations (OpenAI/Codex then Claude) through a brand-new generic AgentRuntime, immediately followed by this third-party review request, is a recursive self-review loop: infrastructure built primarily to critique infrastructure, consuming the same 'bounded worker' budget that could have attempted one real gameplay ticket.

Seven-plus distinct 'truth' surfaces for one linear workflow (task contracts, reconciliation snapshots, GDD RAG, evidence records, current_conformance, execution_authority, AgentRuntime/TaskExecution audit artifacts) is a lot of authority boundaries to reason about before any of them has been exercised on new work.
Provider-scoped output namespacing, resumability, and convenience 'latest' pointers for ArchitectureReview are polish on a diagnostic tool, not on the game-development critical path.
missing_components: A write-capable execution path (even a narrow, single-branch, human-supervised one) — nothing in AgentRuntime can currently modify the repository.
An automated or semi-automated evidence-record generator invoked at the end of a real delivery, rather than hand-authored JSON.
Any implemented consumer of TaskExecution / ExecutionCrew — the design exists in ADRs but has never run.
A lightweight, scoped GDD-change-impact mechanism distinct from the full Reconciliation Verification Crew, needed once real implementation work is interleaved with an iterating GDD.

A single proven example of the full target loop (ready task -> claimed -> implemented -> GER/Unity-validated -> merged -> evidence recorded -> conformant) under the current schema; NSC-023's evidence was retrofitted onto work done outside this pipeline.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary: separating mutable Tasks/*.yaml definitions from immutable evidence/conformance truth, because the prior collapsed model was demonstrably exploitable.
Necessary: reading authority from committed Git HEAD rather than working tree, since it closes an obvious spoofing vector for uncommitted 'evidence.'

Questionable/duplicative: AgentInvocationRequest (generic) vs. TaskExecutionRequest (NSC-specific, unimplemented) vs. execution_authority.py (dispatch gate) vs. current_conformance.py (evidence truth) are four separate modules whose boundaries have only been exercised by having three of them return blanket 'not enabled/denied' — the real cost/benefit of this decomposition is unproven until at least one task flows through all of them.

The Reconciliation layer's 'propose deltas, never directly mutate the graph' boundary (ADR-026) is sound in principle but currently has no lightweight path for small, routine GDD edits, only the full independently-verified bootstrap-grade process — this will likely be bypassed informally (manual Tasks/*.yaml edits) the first time a small GDD wording change needs to ripple through, undermining the boundary in practice.
gdd_iteration_concerns: Reconciliation is explicitly framed and built for one-time bootstrap correctness (immutable snapshot + independent multi-model verification + human approval) — appropriate rigor for seeding 37 initial records once, but far too heavy to re-run for each GDD edit during iterative design, and no lighter-weight scoped-impact mechanism has been implemented despite the docs acknowledging the need.

NSC-003 already demonstrates the moving-target problem in miniature: the persisted contract says decomposition is 'concrete,' but current human-facing guidance says several design questions (input ownership, click vs. hold arbitration, restriction semantics) must still be resolved — meaning a 'complete' decomposition can silently go stale as design understanding evolves, with no automatic trigger to re-flag it.

There is no defined cadence or threshold ('material GDD change,' referenced in 00_MASTER_CONTEXT.md) that is operationalized as code; it is currently a human judgment call with no tooling support, so in practice GDD drift versus task-contract staleness will likely go undetected until a human happens to notice.
result.throughput_assessment: Over the entire observed working window (2026-08-21 bootstrap through 2026-08-23, the current date), net new shipped gameplay is zero: the sole conformant task (NSC-023) predates and was built outside this pipeline. All delivered work in that window is planning/evidence/provider infrastructure, most recently two rounds of self-referential ArchitectureReview migration. Because no provider can currently write to the repository, the architecture today cannot compress any gameplay-development timeline at all — it has no path from 'ready task' to 'implemented code.' The deterministic pieces that do exist (Git-hash-bound evidence checks, the Unity clean-test runner, taskcontrol graph queries) are genuinely reusable once a write path and one real ticket close the loop, so the investment is not wasted, but it is currently front-loaded entirely on governance/audit with none of it yet cashed in against actual game features. Claiming this turns "weeks into days" is unsupported by current evidence; the honest claim is that it has turned "an afternoon of gameplay coding into three days of process engineering," and the architecture must reverse that ratio on its very next slice to be credible.
human_intervention_points: Resolving NSC-003's open design/arbitration questions (input ownership, click-vs-hold, restriction/reset semantics) before any worker can receive it.
Approving every reconciliation bootstrap and verification run (one-time so far, but required by design for any future large-scale reseeding).
Providing required Play Mode approval for any conformance record (done manually for NSC-023 by Vincent Liguori).
Merging every PR — no auto-merge exists or is planned before Milestone 3+.
Every dispatch/authorization decision — taskcontrol authorize currently denies 100% of tasks by design.
Deciding product priority among ready/near-ready tasks — reviewers and the graph explicitly are not treated as authoritative for priority.
Hand-authoring delivery/revalidation evidence records, since no generator tool exists yet.

next_slice.title: Close the loop on one real gameplay slice end-to-end, with a human resolving design ambiguity first and a write-capable worker doing the implementation
next_slice.why: Nothing has ever gone from a persisted task contract to a merged, evidenced feature under the current schema/evidence model, and no provider can currently write code at all. Until that loop runs once, all further AgentRuntime/provider/self-review investment is unfalsified speculation about leverage that hasn't been demonstrated even a single time.
deliverables: A short human decision session resolving NSC-003's open input/arbitration/reset questions, and a decision on whether to split it per CURRENT_STATE.md's suggestion (runtime input + pointer projection foundation, separate from movement/restriction/reset).

A narrow write capability added to exactly one provider path (branch-scoped, diff/scope-checked per ADR-006, no capability generalization beyond what this one ticket needs), OR, if that is judged too large for one slice, explicit acknowledgment that this ticket will be implemented directly (as NSC-023 was) and the pipeline's job for this slice is only to validate and evidence it.
Running the resulting implementation through the existing Unity clean-test runner and GER-style runtime validation.

A second real, non-NSC-023 conformance evidence record, ideally produced with less manual JSON-authoring effort than the first, to start proving the evidence step itself can be made cheaper rather than just correct.
next_slice.proof_of_value: A second task (not NSC-023) reaches taskcontrol state == conformant, produced by an implementation that was actually driven by an agent (even partially), with measured elapsed time and manual-step count compared against doing it by hand — establishing whether this pipeline is actually faster than unassisted development yet.

do_not_build_yet: Any further provider-adapter generalization (a third provider, deeper Claude/Codex feature parity, dual-provider launcher, provider comparison pipeline) until one provider has written and shipped one real ticket.

The Milestone 2 bundle (RAG context packs, Progressive Decomposer, Artifact Authority Gate) as a platform, before a near-frontier task has actually demonstrated it needs decomposition or hits a real missing-design wall.
Continuous autonomy, parallel workers, or dependency-derived taskcontrol ready — all explicitly and correctly deferred already; nothing observed here argues for accelerating them.
Any further ArchitectureReview self-review tooling investment (more reviewer roles, more resumability, more provider-scoped polish) beyond what is needed to read this review's own findings.

A general-purpose evidence-record generation framework — build the minimum needed for the second real task first, then generalize only if a second and third example show a common shape worth automating.

alternative_architecture.description: Do not replace the layered contract/evidence/conformance model — it is a reasonable, evidence-motivated response to a real exploit and is largely sound. Instead, temporarily collapse scope: pick one provider, add the minimum write capability scoped to one branch with Git diff/scope checking already implied by ADR-006/007, and wire {agent attempt -> Unity clean-test run -> evidence record} as a single concrete path for one ticket, deferring the generic multi-provider AgentRuntime's further growth until that path is proven.
alternative_architecture.why_better: This is not a different architecture so much as re-sequencing the same one: build the one missing capability (write) that blocks every other claim of leverage, and prove the full loop once on real gameplay work, before adding more audit/self-review layers on top of a production loop that has never executed.

evidence.observation: _FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITIES = {repository_write, approved_command_execution}; _DISALLOWED_TOOLS includes Bash, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit — the live Claude provider cannot modify the repository or run commands.

States 'AgentRuntime approved_command_execution, repository writing, web access... remain unsupported' and that the two most recent completed slices (Stage 4C/4D) were both ArchitectureReview provider migrations, not gameplay work, while taskcontrol ready/authorize remain UNAVAILABLE/DENIED for all tasks.
Flags NSC-003 as 'a strong first gameplay/context-pipeline anchor' as of the same window this document also spent on ArchitectureReview migrations, showing the anchor was named but not acted on.

decomposition_state: concrete and execution_scope: single_agent are asserted in the persisted contract, contradicting CURRENT_STATE.md's later statement that several design/arbitration questions must first be resolved by a human before this task can be handed to a worker.

ADR-019 / 'Current Development Rule' explicitly requires infrastructure to be proven by advancing actual gameplay work rather than becoming a separate project; the two most recent completed stages instead migrated the self-review tool through two providers in sequence.

Contains a working prototype (PlayerMovement, DoorInteractable, PlayerHealth, PlayerMana, IsometricCameraFollow) plus Play Mode tests — the only real shipped gameplay evidence, produced outside the current AgentRuntime/task-contract pipeline (Assignment 6 GER coursework), later retrofitted with a hand-authored Phase 3 evidence record.

Documents the concrete exploit motivating Phase 1-3: 'a one-line YAML edit can mark a dependency complete and unlock downstream work' without proof — a real, previously observed failure mode that the evidence-conformance model correctly addresses.

Multiple full 8-reviewer + synthesis + adversarial-critique runs exist for both Codex and Claude providers within the same short window, indicating repeated investment in self-review infrastructure rather than gameplay execution.

result.biggest_uncertainty: Whether the project intends the very next slice after this review to finally attempt a write-capable path on a real gameplay ticket (in which case the current infrastructure investment is reasonably front-loaded and about to pay off) or whether it will instead proceed to Milestone 2 / further provider generalization (in which case the recursive self-review pattern observed over the last three days will likely continue). This review cannot observe intent beyond the documented 'Immediate Next Goal,' which itself was infrastructure two cycles in a row.
